Subject: POC Capacity Planning - Recap and next steps

Thanks for the call this morning, Alice - really helpful to walk through Novatech's evaluation goals. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we're aligned before we put the POC plan together:

Summary of success criteria (from your notes):
- End-to-end latency for interactive generation <= 250ms p95 for 2k prompt + 512 tokens
- Sustained throughput to support 10 concurrent users (peak simulation: 100 qps for short bursts)
- Cost target: < $0.01 per generated token (goal to compare against current infra)
- Data isolation & retention: logs retained for 30 days, no customer data persisted beyond session except anonymized metrics

POC plan items we propose to deliver:
1) Reserved capacity: carve out 2 reserved GPU instances (A10G-equivalent) for baseline throughput testing during the 2-week POC
2) Autoscaling: enable burst autoscaling policy to allow +2 additional GPU nodes for short spikes (up to 10 minutes)
3) Load tests: we will run scripted load tests simulating 10 concurrent users and a synthetic 100-qps short burst to validate p95 latency and autoscale behavior
4) Observability: we'll enable per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns so your infra team can validate economics
5) Timeline: kickoff next Tuesday (2026-03-30), 2-week run, final review week of 2026-04-13

Questions / asks for your team:
- Can you confirm the dataset/privacy constraints and if we should enable anonymization?
- Do you have an internal contact for procurement (DocuSign + NDA) so we can get reserved capacity approved?
- Any blackout dates during the POC window?

Attachments: novatech_poc_requirements.xlsx (your filled worksheet) - I used your answers to build the plan. Also attaching a short capacity plan PDF for internal ops (redwood_poc_capacity_plan.pdf).

Next steps: If that looks right, I'll schedule a quick 30m kickoff with Connor (ops) and Logan (solutions) and loop in procurement.

Best,

Hey all - quick ops note on the capacity side based on Alice's burst numbers:

- Reserved baseline: we can reserve 2 x A10G-equivalent instances (each ~24 TFLOPS effective) - should cover sustained throughput for the 10 concurrent users and normal QPS.
- Autoscaling: policy we recommend:
  * Scale up trigger: sustained CPU/GPU util > 70% OR queue length > 50 reqs for 30s
  * Scale step: add 1 GPU node, cool-down 60s
  * Max burst nodes: +4 (i.e., baseline 2 + burst 4 = 6 total)
  * Short-burst override: allow temporary concurrency limits to permit up to +6 nodes for up to 3 minutes (this handles Alice's 200 qps 2-3 minute spike)
- Fallback behavior: if autoscale can't provision nodes in time we will route excess to a lower-cost quantized variant (same model family) to avoid request failure; p95 latency may increase but we avoid errors

I can be the ops point for the run and do daily 15-30m check-ins for the first 3 days. I'll bring fine-grain telemetry (per-route p50/p95, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate) and a short playbook for tuning batch sizes and token limits.

Logan - can you confirm the anticipated token cost delta between our baseline and the quantized fallback so we can give Raj an estimate for expected spend in the POC?

-Connor
